status: fixed 2026-10-14 before any brief was written or tried, at the user's request for option 2 (a better controller prompt, judged on a held-out set)
what_is_tuned: only the controller brief (the run profile's controllerBrief, appended to the controller's system prompt in its own 600-token lane). The controller model (pinned Bonsai-8B base, 284a335a, no adapter), the kernel prompt, decoding (temperature 0) and the trigger policy stay fixed.
rule: configs/controller_qualification_v2.json (signed): its conditions, positives, vetoes and keyAdmissible subset, scored from live runs by scripts/score_live_controller.py

development.data: the seed set, oracle and adversary plus random seeds 0-59 (the collect-v3 seeds), null arm, the candidate brief deciding live
development.iteration: briefs are compared on a development subset (seeds 0-14) to save GPU; the chosen brief is then run on all 60 development seeds
development.record: every brief tried is kept in configs/controller_briefs/ with its development score, whether or not it is chosen

heldOut.A: the seed set, random seeds 60-119 only (no oracle or adversary, which would repeat development runs), null arm
heldOut.B: BitAgent's open-gate scenarios (40, none in the seed set), oracle and adversary plus random seeds 0-59, null arm
heldOut.inProcessSize: A: 978 admissible-move execute turns, 101 positive; B: 1,605 turns, 305 positive (in-process counts with no controller)
heldOut.use: each held-out set is run once, with the final brief only, after it is chosen on development data; nothing about a brief changes after

verdict: the brief qualifies the controller only if the v2 conditions pass on held-out A and on held-out B; development scores are reported, never the verdict
